subject: Autoscale exemption request — Q1 load testing & on-call simulations
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@hydraai.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Autoscale exemption request — Q1 load testing & on-call simulations

Team —

HydraAI has a firm commitment to run two multi-hour load windows in early January for their Q1 launch smoke tests. They also want to run our on-call simulation suite (simulated incidents + traffic spikes) against their dedicated pool to validate fallback behavior. The combined plan pushes well beyond the autoscale burst cap we currently enforce for Dedicated customers.

Ask: we need a short-lived autoscale policy exemption to allow HydraAI to burst an additional ~20 A100-equivalent GPUs for up to 72 hours across the us-west-2 dedicated pool. This is a timeboxed request (window: 2027-01-10 00:00 to 2027-01-13 00:00) and Hydra agreed to cover incremental usage per the attached cost estimate.

Why: the on-call sims exercise cross-region failover and KV-cache warmup under realistic token distributions; if we keep throttling at current caps we won't see the failure modes Hydra cares about and the pilot could fail QA. This is both a customer success and an SRE validation opportunity.

Attached: q1-loadtest-plan.pdf (test schedule + traffic profile), capacity-runbook.md (ops playbook), cost-estimate.xlsx.

Immediate asks:
- Hannah: ops runbook review + gating checklist (need by EOD Thu)
- Marcus: capacity carveout approval path + quick estimate of impact on other pilots
- Laura: executive sign-off for exception & contingency (if you can approve, I will send the final Doc with dates)

I can be available on a quick sync at 9:30 if helpful.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Price
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@hydraai.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale exemption request — Q1 load testing & on-call simulations

Thanks Elliot — good write-up. Quick notes from an Ops perspective after a first pass of the runbook:

- Runbook is comprehensive but I want a clearer rollback trigger set (e.g., sustained 5xx > 1% for 10m, GPU OOM rate > 0.1%). Please add thresholds to the "escalation" section.
- We should gate the carveout behind a dedicated canary window (1 hour) before the long-run to validate KV cache behavior.
- If we approve + allocate the 20 GPUs, Ops will need an automated eviction plan to reclaim capacity within 15 minutes if higher-priority enterprise bursts occur.

I can have a proposed gating checklist and the rollback bullets by end of day today. Also looping in Marcus for capacity impacts.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@hydraai.com>, Rachel Ortiz <rachel@cloudops.io>
Date: 2026-12-09T13:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale exemption request — Q1 load testing & on-call simulations

Elliot / Hannah —

I ran a quick capacity model against the us-west-2 pool. High level: granting a 72h +20-GPU burst will increase contention risk for two medium pilots scheduled that same week (we can move one pilot by 48 hours with notice). Approx incremental cost to account: $18k (matches the attached estimate).

Operational ask: we should formalize the exception as a temporary reserved slice with a hard eviction policy (priority = "pilot-exception-2027-01-HYDRA") and an SLO waiver for the window. Dev — can infra create the slice policy and eviction hook? If yes, mark as action INF-7893 in Jira.

From a cross-team perspective, this is low-risk if we accept the following contingency plan:
- Hydra signs DMA confirming they accept the cost + a 2-hour pre-window canary.
- We postpone "Pilot Beta" scheduled for Jan 11 by 48 hours (not ideal, but feasible).
- Ops retains manual override and will trigger eviction on the triggers Hannah lists.

If Laura can ok the waiver for the 72h window, I will prepare the reservation + the infra ticket today.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Dedicated Capacity | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@hydraai.com>, Rachel Ortiz <rachel@cloudops.io>
Date: 2026-12-10T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Autoscale exemption request — Q1 load testing & on-call simulations

Team — thank you for the clear options. Approved with conditions:

1) HydraAI signs the DMA confirming they accept the incremental cost and the 72h timebox. Marcus, please attach the signed DMA to JIRA-INF-7893.
2) Ops gating checklist (Hannah) must be completed and exercised during the 1-hour canary window.
3) Infra (Dev) must create a temporary reserved slice with the eviction hook and a telemetry dashboard (latency, 5xx, GPU OOMs) linked in the runbook.
4) We will not delay other enterprise customers beyond 24h — move the internal pilot only if absolutely necessary.

Marcus: go ahead and create the reservation and post the ticket by COB today. Elliot: once Marcus confirms, send Hydra the signed DMA and a calendar invite for the canary. I will be on-call during the canary window.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
